# Grid Traversal and Data Structure Adaptation

Also called: Adaptive Isosurface Extraction, Hierarchical Grid Traversal

## Overview
This family adapts standard [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) (typically Marching Cubes) to non-uniform or sparse data structures, optimizing memory usage and computational cost by focusing processing only on regions of interest [S1]. It sets itself apart from [uniform grid](#920-uniform-grid.md) methods by replacing the fixed [linear scan](#1779-canonical-enumeration.md) with hierarchical or sparse traversal logic, and from crack-free AMR methods by focusing on the general mechanism of adapting the domain structure (octree, sparse hash) rather than specific boundary stitching algorithms [1247-octree-based-isosurfacing.md], [9981-crack-free-isosurface-extraction-from-amr-data.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md) (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers. The core mechanism involves traversing the grid cells and evaluating the data to determine which parts of the domain constitute the surface [G].

1.  **Domain Traversal**: The algorithm iterates over the volume data structure [G]. For regular grids, this often involves checking each cell or voxel [G].
2.  **Surface Determination**: A criterion is applied to identify surface locations. In isosurface methods, this involves comparing scalar values against a threshold (isovalue) to detect sign changes or equality [30-isosurface-extraction.md]. In [blocky meshing](#31-blocky-meshing.md), this involves checking occupancy states or material IDs to identify exposed boundaries [31-blocky-meshing.md].
3.  **Primitive Generation**: Geometric primitives (vertices, edges, faces) are generated based on the determined surface locations [G].
4.  **Mesh Coherence**: Adjacent primitives are merged or connected to form a coherent mesh, often requiring vertex merging to avoid duplicates and ensure watertightness [30-isosurface-extraction.md].

## Subtopics

### [Marching Cubes with Octree](1259-marching-cubes-with-octree.md)
Extracts a manifold triangle mesh from an implicit scalar field defined over an adaptive [octree structure](#2792-octree-based-structures.md), replacing the [uniform grid traversal](#9652-uniform-grid-traversal.md) of standard Marching Cubes with a hierarchical domain traversal [1259-marching-cubes-with-octree.md]. It sets itself apart from [Sparse Marching Cubes](3825-sparse-marching-cubes.md) by operating on a pointerless octree structure that adapts resolution based on a split predicate, and from [Hierarchical Marching Cubes Enumeration](5223-hierarchical-marching-cubes-enumeration.md) by relying on a specific domain object (`MC_Domain`) to handle the geometric mapping between octree nodes and cube vertices [1259-marching-cubes-with-octree.md].

### [Sparse Marching Cubes](3825-sparse-marching-cubes.md)
Generates a triangle mesh from a sparse set of 3D points with associated scalar values (e.g., [Signed Distance Fields](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)), avoiding the memory overhead of dense 3D grids [3825-sparse-marching-cubes.md]. It differs from standard Marching Cubes by dynamically [gathering](#9569-gathering.md) corner values for active voxels via lookup, rather than iterating over a fixed dense volume [3825-sparse-marching-cubes.md].

### [Hierarchical Marching Cubes Enumeration](5223-hierarchical-marching-cubes-enumeration.md)
Is a [recursive octree traversal](#2632-recursive-octree-traversal.md) algorithm that extracts isosurface meshes by enumerating voxel faces, edges, and vertices, delegating the actual geometry generation to a standard Marching Cubes routine at leaf nodes [5223-hierarchical-marching-cubes-enumeration.md]. It differs from [Marching Cubes with Octree](1259-marching-cubes-with-octree.md) and [Sparse Marching Cubes](3825-sparse-marching-cubes.md) by explicitly separating the traversal logic into specialized functions for faces, edges, and vertices to ensure coherent mesh generation across hierarchical boundaries [5223-hierarchical-marching-cubes-enumeration.md].

### [2D Stitching](10249-2d-stitching.md)
An index-based tessellation scheme that fills gaps between dual grids of different AMR levels using 'stitch cells' to merge levels seamlessly without subdividing boundary elements [10249-2d-stitching.md].

## Background
The need for [adaptive grid traversal](#10325-grid-traversal-and-data-structures.md) arises from the inefficiency of uniform grids when representing complex geometries or sparse data. Standard Marching Cubes requires $O(N^3)$ memory and computation for a grid of size $N$, which is prohibitive for high-resolution volumes where the surface occupies only a small fraction of the domain [G]. Early work on adaptive isosurfacing focused on octree structures to provide hierarchical refinement [1259-marching-cubes-with-octree.md]. Subsequent developments introduced sparse data structures to handle point-cloud-derived fields like Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) without allocating memory for empty space [3825-sparse-marching-cubes.md]. To address the topological inconsistencies (cracks) inherent in non-uniform grids, specialized traversal algorithms were developed to ensure manifold continuity across level boundaries [5223-hierarchical-marching-cubes-enumeration.md].
